title: The Sixth R: Regenerate
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: A source-to-book picture that shows what the proposed sixth R, regenerate, adds to the 5Rs: the right to rebuild an intelligent textbook from its course description, learning graph, and agentic skills.

educational.topic: The proposed sixth R, regenerate, and the source behind an AI-built textbook
learningObjectives: The learner will explain how the proposed sixth R, regenerate, differs from the 5Rs, using the source and the book on the poster.
prerequisites: The meaning of an intelligent textbook and a learning graph from [Chapter 18](../../chapters/18-components-publishing-oer/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a reference picture, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: Can I recreate it from its source?
Which parts of the source are published with the book?
commonMisconceptions: An open license on the rendered book is enough to rebuild the book
Regenerate is one of Wiley's original 5Rs
Regenerate means hand-editing the text again
assessmentOpportunities: An author posts a textbook under an open license but keeps the learning graph and skills private. Which right is missing?
A teacher translates one chapter of an open textbook by hand. Is that regenerate?
Is regenerate one of David Wiley's original 5Rs?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz buttons
controls.description: switch between exploring the poster and answering quiz questions.

controls.name: Poster zones
controls.description: hover or press to read about that part of the poster. In quiz mode a press is your answer.

controls.name: Try Again
controls.description: repeats the quiz after the last question.
